alex: Quick follow-up to the attn-opt RFC thread — we need to lock on an operational approach for kernel surface and maintenance burden. TL;DR: perf wins for CUTLASS on A100 fp16/TF32, Triton gives faster iteration + portability. Need concrete owners + experiments to decide where we ship first and what falls back.
sasha: +1. My read: CUTLASS is higher perf for common shapes but requires more C++ infra and review cycles. Triton lets us iterate with python kernels and get shop-wide reuse. Tradeoffs: perf vs maintenance velocity.
riya: Agree. Two practical constraints: 1) model catalog (short-seq vs long-seq) distribution, 2) rollout complexity for Dedicated/Private (we can't force users to compile kernels). We should aim to have a runtime adapter that can switch variants per model/route.
chris: Proposal: implement a KernelAdapter interface (small), with methods: `init(device, config)`, `run(attn_args)`, `supports(shape, dtype)` and a metadata file for capabilities. Then we can wire adapter selection into smart routing.
alex: Exactly. Minimal interface keeps runtime simple. Also: perf matrix we ran last week (A100 v100 L4): CUTLASS wins 15-40% for kv-cache heavy loops, Triton is within 5-10% for short seqs and much easier to maintain. We should prioritize CUTLASS for critical paths with an adapter shim.
riya: Ops note: CUTLASS kernels will require nightly build and stricter CI (gcc, nvcc versions). That increases SRE/infra load. Can we gate CUTLASS variants behind Dedicated-only or opt-in flags initially?
sasha: We can gate. Action item: add `variant_policy` to model config (values: auto, prefer-cutlass, prefer-triton, fallback) and use canary flags per customer.
